title: Autonomous DDIL edge PED node with sensor-to-map exploitation (georegistered drone video, minute-scale 3D and change overlays without reach-back) and resilient reconciliation to AIDP/Maven
scoring_notes: Scores are analytical heuristics, not facts. Evidence base is the G13 Gap Evidence Card (gaps/G13.json) plus the three skeptic verdicts; no fresh web calls were made this session, so every claim carries the card's own label (FACT/INFERENCE/RECALL) and confidence. Contract ceilings (TurbineOne $98.9M, Vantor $217M, MSS ~$1.3B) are ceilings, not revenue; the AIDP-Next award has not been made as of 2026-09-24 (responses were due 12 Aug 2026; award projected ~Q1 FY2027) so any statement about who wins it is INFERENCE.

scores.rationale: Real but not mission-fatal in documented form: MIPB 'Swivel Chair War' (NTC 26-02, 2026) documents hand-plotting and NIPR/SIPR re-entry (FACT, HIGH), the AIDP-Next CfS writes a fresh 72-hour DDIL + MSS-exchange requirement (FACT, HIGH), and WSJ/CSIS show connectivity-dependent PED breaking (RECALL, MEDIUM); but no DOT&E/GAO/after-action document names a product failing this requirement (card: 'Public evidence insufficient', LOW). Painful, not yet proven decisive.

Every disconnected rotation, Scarlet Dragon event and MDTF exercise reproduces the wait-for-reach-back / hand-plot cycle (INFERENCE from MIPB and the CfS language, MEDIUM), and LSCO doctrine assumes DDIL; but in garrison and most CTC rotations reach-back still exists, so the pain is episodic rather than daily for most S2 shops.

Money exists around the problem but not for a discrete product: FY27 AIDP RDT&E request $34.830M and Army geospatial $14.764M (search-summary of BA 5D J-book, PDF not opened, MEDIUM), TITAN initial production orders $192M (FACT, HIGH), MSS ceiling ~$1.3B (ceiling, not obligation). The card itself states 'No dedicated line item for an edge PED node exists'; funding would have to be carved out of a prime's award, SBIR/STRATFI or unit O&M.

Score of 1 explained: the only vehicle that names this requirement (AIDP-Next CfS via Army Open Solicitation CSO, ACC-APG) is scoped to a single-foundation enterprise-to-edge continuum, i.e., a prime-sized award; the sensor-to-map half has no solicitation at all (card search for SBIR/xTech topics on sUAS 3D/change detection/ATAK edge returned nothing useful); buyers are split across PM IS&A, PEO Soldier/PM UAS, PEO STRI, CDAO and SOCOM so no contracting officer owns the end-to-end pipeline. The PROBLEM->USER->REQUIREMENT OWNER->PROGRAM OFFICE->CONTRACTING OFFICE->BUDGET->VEHICLE chain exists only for the prime (AIDP-Next), not for a startup selling the glue - this triggers the major penalty.

The unclassified pipeline is feasible today with open components: MISB 0601 KLV parsing, Jetson Orin-class compute, fast MVS/Gaussian-splatting reconstruction (2023+), CRDT/log-based stores, CoT/TAK data packages, OGC 3D Tiles/STAC (card why_now and technical_wedge, INFERENCE, MEDIUM-HIGH). Not a 5 because minute-scale georegistration accuracy on uncalibrated commercial airframes and low-false-alarm change detection at the edge remain unproven by this team, and the AIDP/MSS reconciliation half cannot be engineered without non-public schemas.

Card's own proof-of-concept estimate is $150-300k (2 founders + 1 CV/geospatial engineer, 2 drones, Jetson, 6 months) - i.e., $250k covers only the commodity half; the credible military demo is $1.5-3M and first production deployment $8-20M (INFERENCE from comparable rounds: Reveal $30M Series B, TurbineOne $36M round; not verified). Two 'fatal if absent' specialist hires (photogrammetry/SLAM and CRDT/DDIL distributed systems) are not fundable on $250k for long.

An unclassified commercial-drone demo (georegistration vs RTK truth, time-to-overlay, scripted 72h reconciliation into a mock PostGIS/STAC enterprise) is achievable in 3-6 months, but the card's MVP section concedes it 'does not yet' include AIDP/MSS integration, which 'requires program access'; a demo that the requirement owner would find credible is therefore 12-24 months away (entry_vehicle sequence months 9-24) and gated on an award.

Commercial MISB-tagged drone video, public MISB/STANAG 4609 sample streams, open terrain (USGS 3DEP, Copernicus, Cesium/OSM), VisDrone/xView/DOTA labels and ATAK-CIV/TAK Server public releases are freely obtainable (FACT, HIGH); but the differentiating data - military FMV, the AIDP/MSS data model, the HYDRA API (specification not public) and TITAN interfaces - are obtainable only inside an SBIR Phase II/OTA/CRADA and may be export-controlled, which further constrains the non-U.S.-person founder (needs counsel).

Low burden for the commercial-drone/ATAK-CIV MVP, but the card rates the full thesis 'medium' rising to 'high': ISR exploitation software specially designed for military use may fall under USML Cat XI or EAR 600-series (classification needs counsel), SIPR/IL5 ATO and facility clearance are required for real AIDP/TITAN integration, TAK Product Center review gates military plugin distribution, SBIR requires >50% U.S.-citizen/PR ownership and control (armysbir.army.mil; 13 CFR 121.702), and FOCI rules treat even a green-card holder as a foreign interest (32 CFR 117.11). No legal determination is made here.

The sensor-to-map half and a simulated-DDIL reconciliation test can be built entirely on commercial hardware, open data and open standards (card mvp.uses); this is the thesis's strongest founder-side property. Not a 5 because the differentiating half (conflict-free reconciliation with the real AIDP/MSS) cannot be proven unclassified, so 'start unclassified' does not extend to 'finish unclassified'.

Score of 1 explained: every layer is occupied by funded, arrived firms - Palantir (AIDP incumbent, TITAN prime $127M, MSS owner), Anduril (TITAN hardware $65M, Lattice, NGC2 lead), TurbineOne (edge inference, $98.9M-ceiling Army IDIQ Sept 2025 + JIOP Apr 2026), Reveal (edge 3D, $33.6M STRATFI, SOCOM use claimed since 2021, Series B 2025), Edgybees (georegistration, USAF multi-award), Skydio (on-drone 3D + offline ATAK CoT as a stock X10D feature, Army RQ-28A replacement 2025), Vantor (OWT 3D Tiles, Luno B change detection). All FACT/HIGH per the card except company deployment claims (company marketing, MEDIUM).

Score of 1 explained: incumbents are not weak, distracted or exiting; the AIDP-Next CfS obliges the winner to build the 72h DDIL edge and MSS sync as core scope, and the card judges TurbineOne/Reveal/Anduril could add KLV ingest and store-and-forward sync in well under six months on open standards (INFERENCE, MEDIUM). The only vulnerability is structural disinterest in vendor-neutrality, which is a reason the seam is unclaimed rather than a reason incumbents can be displaced.

TAK/CoT and data packages are government-owned and open enough for plugins (FACT, HIGH), and 3D Tiles/STAC/GeoPackage are open; but the interfaces that matter for the thesis - AIDP/MSS data models (Palantir-controlled today), HYDRA (CPE ISW, spec not public), TITAN and drone-OEM ground stations - are vendor- or government-gated, and the edge-to-enterprise sync seam will be controlled by the AIDP-Next winner (award pending).

Score of 1 explained: the card's own defensibility section states the algorithms (splatting, CRDTs, change detection) are open and that every proprietary asset (AIDP/MSS/TITAN/HYDRA adapters, TAK-certified footprint, IL5 accreditation, soldier-validated workflow) 'is also exactly what the AIDP-Next prime can reproduce or gate'; a moat exists only if the government designates the sync layer as an open, government-owned interface, which is HYPOTHESIS with no supporting evidence.

Drone-agnostic offline georegistration/3D/change detection has real analogues in wildfire, SAR, disaster response (ATAK-CIV/TAK users), infrastructure inspection, mining and allied civil protection (card: 'medium'); but commercial buyers already run Skydio/DJI/DroneDeploy/Pix4D cloud workflows, so the offline/DDIL value proposition is strongest only for remote-industrial and public-safety niches.

If a vendor-neutral sensor-to-map layer took hold, adjacencies exist (SOF, NGC2 edge, allied ATAK users such as UK/NATO SOF, Bundeswehr D-LBO/TaWAN via the German founder, Ukraine Delta/Kropyva-style split systems per CSIS 2024) - but each adjacency has its own entrenched vendors (Quantum Systems/Helsing/ARX in Germany; Reveal already claims UK and Ukraine users) and export licensing of a U.S.-developed ISR exploitation product needs counsel; the card calls allied sales 'a later-stage add-on, not a reason to start'.

Per-node/per-device software licensing and adapter maintenance could recur, but there is no O&M or sustainment line a startup can bill against; revenue would arrive as sub-awards from a prime, SBIR phases or unit-level purchases, none of which is a documented recurring stream (INFERENCE, LOW). TITAN and AIDP recurring spend flows to Palantir/Anduril.

Score of 1 explained: three of the card's six required roles are 'fatal if absent' and none is on the team - a photogrammetry/SLAM/neural-3D engineer, a CRDT/DDIL distributed-systems engineer, and a former 35F/12Y/SOF intel NCO with recent NTC/JRTC or TiC experience - plus defense/export counsel; the primary entry vehicle (SBIR/xTech) applies a >50% U.S.-citizen/PR ownership-and-control test that the Indonesian founder's equity cannot satisfy and the German founder's satisfies only once permanent residency is actually issued (13 CFR 121.702; armysbir.army.mil); AFWERX FAQ (AFRL-2025-3235, 2025-07-02) limits foreign-national participation on DoD SBIR work to public-domain/fundamental research; clearances are citizen-only and FOCI mitigation would follow a facility clearance. Two students with $250k cannot buy their way past these constraints in the timeframe the incumbents set. Constraints described for counsel review, not legal conclusions.

market.summary: No dedicated budget line for an edge PED node or sensor-to-map middleware; money flows through AIDP-Next, TITAN production ($192M initial orders) or SBIR/STRATFI, all prime- or program-shaped. Both technical halves have funded occupants (TurbineOne $98.9M-ceiling IDIQ; Reveal $33.6M STRATFI; Skydio X10D onboard 3D + offline ATAK; Edgybees USAF award). The reconciliation seam is written into the AIDP-Next CfS for the winner to build. Buyer fragmentation across five offices means no contracting officer can buy the pipeline. Failure-mode evidence is thin (one CfS text, one MIPB anecdote). SBIR ownership test and controlled-data access make founder fit near-fatal. The card's own incumbent_response already says 'largely reject as a standalone company thesis'. Analyst assessment: ACCEPTED - every factual pillar is sourced in the card; the only soft spot is that 'most likely Palantir wins AIDP-Next' is INFERENCE (award pending), which does not change the conclusion because whoever wins is obliged to build the seam.

competition.summary: Every piece - edge inference (TurbineOne), edge 3D (Reveal), georegistration (Edgybees), on-drone 3D + offline CoT (Skydio, now stock on the Army's company-level drone) - has a more advanced occupant; AIDP/MSS is Palantir's product and the AIDP-Next winner is contractually asked to build the 72h DDIL sync; Anduril (Lattice/Klas/NGC2) and L3Harris (HYDRA, TITAN sub) can bundle equivalents; open standards mean no technical moat and incumbents could add KLV ingest + CRDT sync in under six months. Analyst assessment: ACCEPTED, with two caveats - the 'Palantir brands AIDP on palantir.com' claim is RECALL not re-verified, and the sub-six-month copy estimate is INFERENCE (MEDIUM); neither weakens the core point that the seam is owned by the pending prime award.

feasibility.summary: Chicken-and-egg access problem: the differentiator (real AIDP/MSS reconciliation) cannot be built or demonstrated outside a program, so the fundable MVP is the commodity half already occupied by Skydio/Reveal/Edgybees. Founder-fit is severely constrained by 13 CFR 121.702 (SBIR >50% U.S. ownership/control), AFWERX foreign-national limits (AFRL-2025-3235), citizen-only clearances (EO 12968/SEAD 4) and FOCI (32 CFR 117.11). Capital mismatch: $1.5-3M for a credible demo and $8-20M for deployment vs $250k; 3+ year runway to revenue-relevant deployment. Defensibility weak by the card's own admission. Analyst assessment: ACCEPTED - the regulatory citations match E07 and the card's regulatory_burden section; the clearance-timeline arithmetic (2031-2032) is INFERENCE that depends on when the green card is actually issued but the direction is right.

verdict_rationale: Killed as scoped. Decisive reason: there is no identifiable PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> CONTRACT VEHICLE path for a discrete startup product. The chain exists (Army G-2/USAICoE -> PM IS&A -> ACC-APG -> FY27 AIDP RDT&E $34.8M request / TITAN production -> AIDP-Next CfS) but it terminates in a prime-sized single-foundation award whose winner is obliged to build the 72-hour DDIL edge and MSS exchange (FACT, HIGH: intelligencecommunitynews.com 2026-07-24; CPE ISW industry-day slides 2026-03), not in a line a two-founder company can sell into. Every technical layer is already occupied by a funded, arrived vendor (TurbineOne $98.9M-ceiling IDIQ 2025-09-04 and JIOP 2026-04-16; Reveal $33.6M STRATFI 2024-04; Skydio X10D onboard 3D and offline ATAK CoT; Edgybees USAF award; Palantir/Anduril TITAN production $192M 2026-09-01), the algorithms are open, and the card's own defensibility section says every proprietary asset is reproducible or gateable by the AIDP-Next prime. Founder fit compounds this: the primary entry vehicle (SBIR) applies an ownership-and-control test the current cap table cannot obviously pass, the differentiating data (military FMV, AIDP/MSS schemas, HYDRA API) is reachable only inside an award, and three 'fatal if absent' roles are missing. All three skeptics refuted with strength 5/4/4; I find no evidence that rebuts any of them - the gap card's own incumbent_response ('largely reject as a standalone company thesis') anticipates their conclusion. The narrower drone-agnostic TAK-plugin version is recorded below as an option, but it is a different, non-C4ISR-primary thesis (a public-safety/TAK-ecosystem tool competing with features Skydio ships free) and does not rescue G13 as a defense market gap; it should be evaluated on its own merits under the dual-use track, not credited to G13.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not recommended as a survivor of G13, but recorded for completeness (all three skeptics converge on it): drop the AIDP/MSS reconciliation ambition and all military-FMV dependence; build only a drone-agnostic MISB 0601 KLV -> georegistered footprint / incremental 3D Tiles / change-vs-baseline overlay pipeline as an ATAK-CIV plugin plus headless Jetson edge service, on commercial drones, open terrain and unclassified data (EAR99 architecture to be confirmed by counsel); sell first to public-safety/SAR/wildfire/infrastructure-inspection users of TAK where offline operation is valued; pursue a TAK Product Center plugin listing, xTech/AFWERX open topic, or a JIOP/Scarlet Dragon touchpoint only as slow-burn optionality once a U.S.-citizen-controlled cap table and a clearable field engineer exist; treat acquisition or onboarding by TurbineOne/Reveal/Skydio/the AIDP-Next winner as the primary exit. Why this still does not earn 'borderline': the sensor-to-map half ships as a stock feature on the Army's chosen company-level drone (Skydio X10D), the commercial market already runs cloud workflows (Skydio/DJI/DroneDeploy/Pix4D), and the moat is limited to integration drudgery that any of the named incumbents can replicate in months - it is a feature business, not a company-shaped gap.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this space, the only thing worth building first is the narrow unclassified slice: a headless Jetson Orin edge service plus ATAK-CIV plugin that ingests any MISB 0601 KLV stream (Skydio, Parrot, PX4-class airframes), georegisters the footprint against an open baseline (USGS 3DEP/Copernicus/Cesium), produces incremental 3D Tiles and change-vs-baseline overlays within minutes fully offline, and keeps a CRDT-backed local store that reconciles into a mock PostGIS/STAC enterprise after a scripted 72-hour, 5%-bandwidth outage with zero lost or duplicated records - roughly $150-300k and 6 months with one hired photogrammetry engineer. They would show it to a JIOP/Scarlet Dragon-type soldier touchpoint (XVIII Airborne Corps route that TurbineOne used), a brigade S2/12Y geospatial cell on a TiC rotation, and, for the dual-use fallback, a wildfire/SAR ATAK-CIV user. The demonstration would prove measurable georegistration error against RTK ground truth, time-to-overlay in minutes, an acceptable change-alert false-alarm rate, and deterministic 72-hour reconciliation with provenance - things the incumbents assert but do not publish. The customer would care because today the S2 either waits hours-to-days for enterprise products over a congested link or hand-plots and re-enters data when disconnected (MIPB 'Swivel Chair War', NTC 26-02). Why this fails the crush test: the airframe the Army standardized on already builds 3D on-drone and streams CoT offline (Skydio), Reveal already sells offline edge 3D to SOCOM/Army with STRATFI money, TurbineOne already holds the edge-inference IDIQ, and the reconciliation endpoint that would make the demo genuinely different (real AIDP/MSS/HYDRA) is non-public and about to be owned by the AIDP-Next winner, who is contractually asked to build the same sync layer - so the incumbent does not need to crush the startup, it only needs to ship its own version of the plumbing inside an award it already holds. The milestone that would justify $2-5M would be a signed SBIR Direct-to-Phase-II/DIU CSO/OTA that grants access to military FMV and an AIDP or HYDRA interface plus a written soldier-touchpoint result showing an S2 adopted the tool without a field service engineer; on the current evidence, cap table and access constraints, I do not believe that milestone is reachable on $250k before the AIDP-Next award (~Q1 FY2027) forecloses the seam, which is why the gap is killed.
bear_case_summary: Both technical halves (edge inference: TurbineOne $98.9M-ceiling IDIQ; edge 3D: Reveal $33.6M STRATFI, SOCOM use claimed) and the sensor-to-map layer (Skydio X10D stock features, Edgybees georegistration) are occupied; the reconciliation seam is written into the AIDP-Next CfS as prime scope and the enterprise endpoint (AIDP/MSS) is vendor-controlled; there is no dedicated budget line and no contracting office owns the end-to-end pipeline; algorithms and standards are open so the moat is integration drudgery a well-funded incumbent can replicate in months; SBIR ownership/control, clearance and FOCI constraints plus three missing 'fatal if absent' roles make the team unable to reach the controlled data needed for the differentiator; $250k covers only the commodity half against a $1.5-3M credible-demo requirement. The card's own authors reach the same conclusion.
bull_case_summary: The pain is real and freshly codified: the Army wrote 72-hour DDIL autonomous edge operation and bi-directional MSS exchange into the AIDP-Next CfS (July 2026), MIPB documents swivel-chair workarounds at NTC 26-02, CDAO lists edge data integration as unfinished work, and TITAN Basic production ($192M initial) shows the Army paying for lighter forward nodes. No incumbent is documented as delivering a drone-agnostic, standards-based (KLV/CoT/3D Tiles/STAC) pipeline with change detection and conflict-free reconciliation; incumbents have structural disincentives to be vendor-neutral; the unclassified MVP is buildable on commercial hardware and open data in six months; the Army's company-level standardization on MISB/CoT-emitting drones (Skydio X10D) and Jetson-class compute make minute-scale edge 3D newly feasible; TAK is a government-owned, plugin-friendly distribution channel; and allied ATAK users (UK, NATO SOF) plus German routes are later adjacencies. If the government were to designate the edge-sync interface as open and government-owned, a first-mover implementer could become the default adapter.
confidence_note: HIGH that G13 as scoped is not a credible standalone opportunity for this team: the incumbent awards, TITAN production decision, AIDP-Next CfS requirement and SBIR eligibility rules are FACT/HIGH in the card and uncontested by any skeptic. MEDIUM on secondary points: the identity of the AIDP-Next winner (INFERENCE, award pending), Reveal/Skydio deployment claims (company statements), the sub-six-month incumbent copy estimate (INFERENCE), and FY27 budget figures (search-summary of the J-book, PDF not opened). No web calls were made this session; 'RECALL - not re-verified this session' applies to the CDAO Open DAGIR, WSJ/CSIS and palantir.com claims.
